labels.label: bzthm:c2s3t2_poche_balayable_affine
labels.notes: I read the paper block (benzecri1960_ch2.tex l.627-646, checked against the scan, p. 256 = PDF p. 29: 1°-4° as transcribed, and no « induisant φ sur P » in the affine 1°) against the projective statement l.517-533 and its proof l.535-622. Hypotheses. theoreme_poche_balayable_affine and theoreme_deuxieme/troisieme/quatrieme_affine assume [ChartedSpace (Fin n → ℝ) V] [HasGroupoid V (affGroupoid n)] [PreconnectedSpace V], IsBalayable (GAR n) (Fin n → ℝ) V (GAR n = all affine equivalences of ℝⁿ, IsBalayable = IsBalayableFor ⊤, Déf. 15) and IsPocheAff P φ z (Déf. 1). That is weaker than the paper's variété: there is no T2 and no second countability, and V need only be preconnected. Every n is covered, with no NeZero. The 3° and 4° lemmas quantify over every developing p with EqOn p φ P. That is at least as strong as the paper's chart φ̃, which is unique (IsDeveloping.eq_of_eqOn_poche_affine). Conclusions. 2° is SimplyConnectedSpace P → SimplyConnectedSpace V, which is the paper's. 3° is IsCoqueAff → Convex ℝ (range φ̃). Déf. 2 is φ(P) convex, and the conclusion is the paper's « un convexe » (= IsAffConvex). 4° is IsCoqueStricteAff → ¬ ContainsAffLine (range φ̃), with ContainsAffLine = ∃ A, (∃ p w, w ≠ 0 ∧ A = range (t ↦ t•w +ᵥ p)) ∧ A ⊆ C. That is « ne contient pas de droite ». No hypothesis is added, and none is vacuous. Printed forms. TheoremeAffinePrinted (V : Type, T2, Connected, SecondCountable, IsBalayable, IsPocheAff) is the printed affine Theorem. 1° reads P = φ̃⁻¹({z<1} ∩ range φ̃), which equals φ̃⁻¹{z<1}, so it is l.632-633 literally. It adds « induisant φ sur P » (EqOn), a stronger conclusion disclosed in SCOPE. The literal reading follows from it (TheoremeAffinePrinted.literal). I compared TheoremeComposanteAffinePrinted with TheoremeAffinePrinted conjunct by conjunct: they differ ONLY in 1°c, with (∀ x ∈ P, P = connectedComponentIn (φ̃⁻¹{z<1}) x) in place of P = φ̃⁻¹({z<1} ∩ range φ̃). Chart, source = univ, EqOn, 2°, 3° and 4° are identical. theoremeAffinePrinted_iff (TheoremeAffinePrinted n ↔ ConnexeAffinePrinted n) is not a tautology. → goes through premierAffinePrinted_iff and the uniqueness of the developing map. ← needs the unconditional 2°-4° and poche_eq_preimage_iff_affine. ConnexeAffinePrinted is a genuine open connectedness statement (OQ-75), proved for n ≤ 1. OQ-75, plainly: YES, the component-form answer marks the row with no change to any Lean declaration. theoremeComposanteAffinePrinted is proved for every n, with no sorry and standard axioms, and it is the printed Theorem with 1°c in component form. The only edit is the mark itself: the label line of this module docstring becomes **`bzthm:c2s3t2_poche_balayable_affine`**, and the « Not marked » sentence goes. Under the full-form answer, the mark waits on a proof of ConnexeAffinePrinted. No mark appears anywhere in the file (checked with the ledger's own regex docstring_label_re on the whole file, not only the first 4000 characters). That is correct for a `partial` row with OQ-75 open, as the dispatch requires. Non-vacuity. theoreme_poche_balayable_affine_demiEspace (V = {x₀ > 0} ⊂ ℝⁿ⁺¹, P = {0 < x₀ < 1} ≠ V, z = x₀ non-constant) meets every hypothesis of 1°-3°: IsPocheAff, a convex φ(P), isBalayable_demiEspaceOuvert, P simply connected. demiEspaceOuvert n is Connected, T2 and SecondCountable by instance, which I checked by probe, so the printed forms' hypotheses also hold. theoreme_poche_balayable_affine_demiDroite (]0,∞[, the strict shell ]0,1[ ≠ V) meets every hypothesis of 1°-4°: a strict shell, P simply connected, GA(1)-sweepable, preconnected; T2 and SecondCountable by instance. Its conclusions include the full form, V simply connected, a convex φ̃(V) and no line. The defeq step is sound. demiDroiteOuverte and demiEspaceOuvert 0 are the same Opens ⟨{x | 0 < x 0}, isOpen_lt continuous_const (continuous_apply 0)⟩ over Fin (0+1) → ℝ ≡ Fin 1 → ℝ. My probe proved `demiDroiteOuverte = demiEspaceOuvert 0 := rfl` and accepted `isBalayable_demiEspaceOuvert 0 : IsBalayable (GAR 1) (Fin 1 → ℝ) demiDroiteOuverte`. The kernel checked it, and the statement stays about demiDroiteOuverte with its own instances. Line citations in the docstrings match the transcription: l.627, 635, 637, 639-640, 596-598, 600-603, 609-619, 181-186, 632-633 and 586.

checks.finding_full_form_for_every_shell: TRUE. poche_eq_preimage_of_coque_affine assumes only [PreconnectedSpace V], IsBalayable (GAR n), IsCoqueAff P φ z, IsDeveloping p and EqOn p φ P. Its proof is the strict poche_eq_preimage_of_convex_affine fed by 3°. Nothing beyond a shell is assumed. The sharpened OQ-75 is right as an upper bound. A constant cote is z ≡ 0, since inf = 0 on a nonempty φ(P), and that case is settled (poche_eq_preimage_of_cote_eq_zero_affine). n ≤ 1 is settled (premierAffinePrinted_of_le_one), and now every shell. So the full form is unproved only for a non-shell pocket with a non-constant cote in n ≥ 2, and even there not when φ̃(V) is star-shaped about a point of cote < 1. The REPORT lists that exclusion too. The curated row already anticipated it (« 3° gives convexity for a shell »); this file proves it.
checks.iff_characterisations: All three are TRUE and NON-TRIVIAL. containsAffLine_range_iff_affine assumes only IsPocheAff: no shell, no strict shell, no line hypothesis. ← is the inclusion φ(P) ⊆ range p. → is the paper's argument, and I checked it by hand. L = q₀ + ℝw ⊆ φ̃(V). g with gM ∈ P (Prop. 7′). A with φ̃∘g = A∘φ̃ (rigidity), so A(L) = φ̃(gM) + ℝ A.linear w ⊆ φ̃(V). Each sub-segment [φ̃(gM), t u + φ̃(gM)] lies in A(L) ⊆ target, so it is a segment of V (isAffSegment_of_chart), and condition b puts its end in P when z < 1. Then z ≥ 0 there (isGLB). z is affine along the line, t ↦ t·z.linear u + z(φ̃ gM). If z.linear u ≠ 0, the parameter giving value −1 contradicts z ≥ 0. So z is constant < 1 and A(L) ⊆ φ(P). isCoqueAff_iff_convex_range_affine: → is 3°; ← is φ(P) = {z<1} ∩ range p, from the full form for a convex range, which is convex. isCoqueStricteAff_iff_range_affine rewrites with the two. The claim that the 4° argument does not use the convexity of φ(P) is borne out by the statement of containsAffLine_range_iff_affine.

findings.what: « open for a non-constant cote in dimension n ≥ 2 (OQ-75) » does not take this file's own result into account. The full form is now proved for every shell (poche_eq_preimage_of_coque_affine).

notes_for_master: No major finding. The four minor items are wording fixes the master can apply at graduation (two lines of the module docstring) or when curating (the REPORT's notes and findings). The `notes` paragraph argues, without formalising it, that OQ-71's full form holds for every projective shell. That is a different row, and it is labelled « ARGUED, NOT FORMALISED ». It was not audited, and it should not reach the author as a fact without a Lean proof. At graduation, as the evidence says, re-point the row's blocked_on to OQ-75 alone.
